tasks.title: Numbering in the process namespace
tasks.statement: Write a function pid_namespaces(procs): procs is a list of processes [number on the host, namespace]. The namespace "host" is the ordinary one: the number inside equals the number on the host. In the other namespaces, processes are numbered anew from 1 in ascending order of their host numbers. Return a dictionary "number on the host (as a string) -> number inside the namespace".
tasks.hint: Sort the processes and keep a counter for each namespace.

tasks.title: A limit with hierarchy
tasks.statement: In cgroups version two, a parent's limit restricts its descendants. Write a function effective_limit(parents, limits, node): parents is a dictionary "group -> parent" (the root has no entry), limits is a dictionary "group -> limit" (not every group has one), node is a group. Return the smallest limit among the group itself and all of its ancestors, or None if there are no limits anywhere.
tasks.hint: Walk up through parents to the root and collect the limits you find.

tasks.title: The overlayfs file system
tasks.statement: Write a function overlay_run(lowers, ops): lowers are the lower layers of the image from top to bottom (dictionaries "path -> contents"). On top lies an empty container layer. The operations are: ["write", path, data] (a write to the top layer), ["delete", path] (if the path exists in the lower layers, a whiteout marker is placed in the top layer, otherwise the path is simply removed from the top layer), and ["read", path] (first the top layer; a whiteout marker hides the file; then the lower layers from top to bottom; if it is nowhere, None). Do not modify the input data. Return the list of results of all the reads.
tasks.hint: Store a special marker value for the whiteout in the top layer.

tasks.title: System call filter
tasks.statement: Write a function seccomp_run(allowed, trace, action): allowed is a list of permitted system calls, trace is the process's calls in order, action is what to do for forbidden ones: "errno" (the call returns an error and the process continues) or "kill" (the process is killed at the first forbidden call). Return a tuple (how many calls were executed, the list of forbidden calls in order; with kill it holds at most one).
tasks.hint: Walk through trace; with kill, stop at the first forbidden call.

tasks.title: Packing density
tasks.statement: Write a function fit_instances(host_mb, reserve_mb, workload_mb, overhead_mb): how many identical instances fit on a host. Each takes workload_mb for the workload and overhead_mb of overhead (small for a container, and for a virtual machine it includes the guest kernel), and reserve_mb is left for the host. Return the integer number of instances (not less than zero).
tasks.hint: (host - reserve) // (workload + overhead), but not less than 0.

tasks.title: Choosing a runtime
tasks.statement: Write a function choose_runtime(req): req is a dictionary with the boolean fields "trusted" (your own trusted code), "needs_other_os" (a non-Linux system is needed), "kernel_modules" (your own kernel modules are needed), and "multi_tenant" (there are other people's tenants on the server). The rules, in order: another OS or kernel modules are needed - "vm"; the code is trusted - "container"; other people's tenants - "kata"; otherwise - "gvisor".
tasks.hint: Check the conditions strictly in the order given.

tasks.title: User mapping
tasks.statement: Write a function map_uid(uid_map, inner): uid_map is the user namespace table, a list of rows [start_inside, start_outside, count], and inner is a user ID inside the container. Return the corresponding ID on the host: if inner falls in the range [start_inside, start_inside + count), the result is start_outside + inner - start_inside. If the ID is not mapped by any row, return None.
tasks.hint: Go through the table rows and find the one whose range contains inner.

tasks.title: gVisor attack surface
tasks.statement: Write a function sentry_split(calls, host_set): calls are the application's system calls, host_set is a list of calls that the Sentry has to pass on to the real host kernel; it handles the rest itself. Return a tuple (how many calls the Sentry handled, how many went to the host, the share handled by the Sentry in whole percent, rounded down; for an empty list, 100).
tasks.hint: Count the calls in host_set and subtract them from the total.
